notes:
Batch AI (lidocaine-topical, capsaicin, menthol-methyl-salicylate-camphor, aescin-diethylamine-salicylate, aescin, diosmin-hesperidin, white-soft-paraffin). All quotes checked FOUND against fetchtext/lib text. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). SEARCHES (2026-10-17): emc search and emc ingredient pages (lidocaine 335/1264/3192, methyl salicylate 762, camphor 192, diethylamine salicylate 42, white soft paraffin 340); MHRA Products search index (product name, substance name and full text); MHRA Drug Safety Update; SPS; BUMPS (no leaflets for lidocaine, capsaicin, emollients, horse chestnut). SUBSTITUTE / NEAREST UK PRODUCTS: (1) lidocaine 2% gel: no single-ingredient lidocaine 2% gel SmPC on emc; the only UK single-ingredient lidocaine hydrochloride 2% gel is an MHRA Products SPC (PL 03377/0003, urethral/rectal gel in pre-filled syringes); used for the clinic 2% gel with a formulation note. Its paediatric weight table did not extract cleanly from the PDF and was not used. (2) capsaicin: clinic product is 0.03%; UK has 0.025% (osteoarthritis) and 0.075% (post-herpetic neuralgia, painful diabetic neuropathy) creams; both recorded as separate formulations. (3) menthol/methyl salicylate/camphor: the only UK cream with all three is a muscle rub that also contains capsicum oleoresin and only 0.42% methyl salicylate; clinic products may contain much more methyl salicylate (strength not given in the clinic list). The rub is NOT added to group salicylate on purpose: that group drives systemic salicylate interactions (insulin, sulfonylureas, diuretics, corticosteroids) which the topical SmPC does not state; the salicylate hypersensitivity contraindication is expressed as an allergy rule with allergen group:salicylate instead. (4) aescin oral: no pure aescin product in the UK; one UK Traditional Herbal Registration (THR) for horse chestnut seed extract gastro-resistant tablets equal to 50 mg triterpene glycosides as beta-aescin; used only for the 50 mg extract formulation (traditional use only). The 20 mg aescin tablet formulation has no UK source and carries no content. NO UK PRODUCT: aescin/diethylamine salicylate gel (no aescin-containing topical product in the UK; diethylamine salicylate exists only alone as a 10% cream, not used); diosmin/hesperidin (no emc result, no MHRA Products document by name, substance or full text for diosmin or hesperidin, no THR); white soft paraffin ointment (no UK SmPC for white soft paraffin alone; it appears only as one component of emollient creams/ointments with other ingredients, not used; MHRA DSU and SPS fire-risk advice for all paraffin-containing emollients is shown, no rules). SPS fire-risk article (June 2026) says fire risk applies to all emollients including paraffin-free ones; MHRA DSU (2018) says risk with all paraffin-containing emollients regardless of concentration and cannot be excluded with paraffin-free ones - consistent. NEW GROUP: amide-local-anaesthetic (lidocaine-topical only). NEW CONDITIONS: methaemoglobinaemia-hereditary-idiopathic, traumatised-mucosa-sepsis-site, venous-leg-ulcer. REUSED CONDITIONS from other batches: renal-impairment (A/C/G/Z), broken-ulcerated-skin (AG), cardiac-conduction-disturbance (E), severe-infection-shock (D), respiratory-failure (D), peanut-soya-allergy (D).
AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent second check, log in audit/AH-AI.md): AESCIN CONVERTED TO no-uk-product. The UK THR 13668/0010 active substance is horse chestnut seed dry extract (MHRA substance Aesculus hippocastanum dry extract 4-6:1), not aescin, so it is a different active substance from the clinic aescin tablets; all sections not-available, rules [], formulations from the clinic list only (ids now aescin-tab-50 and aescin-tab-20). Source mhra-thr-13668-0010-spc is kept here for reference but is no longer quoted; condition venous-leg-ulcer removed (no other user). If the clinic confirms its 50 mg tablet is a horse chestnut seed extract, the previous file is in the audit scratch folder and could be restored. WHITE SOFT PARAFFIN: sections made not-available and rules [] as SCHEMA requires for no-uk-product; the MHRA DSU 2018 and SPS June 2026 fire-risk advice is now summarised in availability.note (sources mhra-dsu-emollients-burns-2018 and sps-emollient-fire-risk kept here for reference, no longer quoted). Lidocaine G6PD rule caution -> info (no action stated in the SPC). Menthol rub formulation note corrected (it is not the only UK cream with the three ingredients; it has a fourth active). The rub is confirmed NOT in group salicylate (local product; the salicylate hypersensitivity contraindication is the allergy rule).
